title: A queue module
description:
Write a module that returns a `Queue` class (first in, first out). The tests load it with `require("solution")`.

| Method | Does |
|---|---|
| `Queue.new()` | an empty queue |
| `q:push(value)` | adds at the back |
| `q:pop()` | removes and returns the value at the front; `nil` when empty |
| `q:peek()` | the front value without removing it; `nil` when empty |
| `q:size()` | how many values are waiting |

`table.remove(t, 1)` moves every other item down, so a queue built on it gets slow when it is long. Keep two numbers instead, the position of the first item and of the last, so that `push` and `pop` do the same small amount of work however long the queue is. The tests push and pop 300,000 values.

solution.solution.lua:
local Queue = {}
Queue.__index = Queue

function Queue.new()
    return setmetatable({ first = 1, last = 0, items = {} }, Queue)
end

function Queue:push(value)
    self.last = self.last + 1
    self.items[self.last] = value
end

function Queue:pop()
    if self.first > self.last then return nil end
    local value = self.items[self.first]
    self.items[self.first] = nil
    self.first = self.first + 1
    return value
end

function Queue:peek()
    if self.first > self.last then return nil end
    return self.items[self.first]
end

function Queue:size()
    return self.last - self.first + 1
end

return Queue

hints: Start with `first = 1, last = 0`: the queue is empty whenever `first > last`.
After taking the front value, set `self.items[self.first] = nil` so the table does not keep it alive, then move `first` on.
rules: Keep first and last positions instead of table.remove, which moves every item.
unitTests:
local Queue = require("solution")

test("first in, first out", function()
    local q = Queue.new()
    q:push("a"); q:push("b"); q:push("c")
    check_eq(q:size(), 3)
    check_eq(q:peek(), "a")
    check_eq(q:pop(), "a")
    check_eq(q:pop(), "b")
    q:push("d")
    check_eq(q:pop(), "c")
    check_eq(q:pop(), "d")
    check_eq(q:size(), 0)
end)

test("empty queues", function()
    local q = Queue.new()
    check_eq(q:pop(), nil)
    check_eq(q:peek(), nil)
    check_eq(q:size(), 0)
    q:push(1)
    q:pop()
    check_eq(q:pop(), nil)
    check_eq(q:size(), 0)
end)

test("queues are separate", function()
    local a, b = Queue.new(), Queue.new()
    a:push(1)
    check_eq(b:size(), 0)
end)

test("long queues stay fast", function()
    local q = Queue.new()
    local n = 300000
    for i = 1, n do q:push(i) end
    local total = 0
    for _ = 1, n do total = total + q:pop() end
    check_eq(total, n * (n + 1) // 2)
    check_eq(q:size(), 0)
end)
